    choice.multinomial_logit¶

    Which product customers choose on each shopping trip: a conditional (multinomial) logit over alternative-specific covariates such as price and promotion, with household-specific product preferences. Uncertainty comes from the Bayesian bootstrap over households; new households draw their preferences from the fitted spread.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference bootstrap
    Representation draws
    Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, forecast, predict
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO invalid: bootstrap draws have no pointwise log-likelihood
    Default plots core.data_overview, core.posterior_forest
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    y_hat (hh, trip, product) probability Choice probability of each product per household and trip (predictive: one sampled choice, one-hot)

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    covariates list of string (optional) null advanced Alternative-specific variables along product (default: every numeric variable with the product dim)
    random_effects list of hh ["hh"] advanced Household-specific product intercepts ([hh]) or none ([]) (max items 1)
    effect_sd number 1.0 advanced Prior sd of the household effects (smaller pools households more) (> 0, ≤ 10)
    coef_sd number 10.0 advanced Prior sd of the product intercepts and coefficients (weak) (> 0, ≤ 1000)
    reference string (optional) null advanced Product whose intercept is fixed at 0 (default: the first label)
    max_iter integer 500 advanced ≥ 10, ≤ 10000
    Input data contract (schema template) 
    {
  "params": {
    "covariates": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "path": "covariates",
      "default": []
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "hh": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "hyperprior"
      },
      "trip": {
        "kind": "index",
        "policy": "extend"
      },
      "product": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "hh",
          "trip"
        ],
        "dtype": "str",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow"
      },
      "{*covariates as v}": {
        "dims": [
          "hh",
          "trip",
          "product"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "covariate",
        "missing": "allow"
      }
    }
  }
}

    mmm.bayesian¶

    mmm-framework's Bayesian marketing-mix model: adstock and saturation per channel, trend and seasonality, national or hierarchical over geos and products, channel effects stated as returns on spend, business priors and lift tests as calibration, budget optimisation with mmm-framework planning.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, forecast, predict
    Contributions additive
    Decision objective yes
    Fast scoring –
    Owns carryover, inverse_units, scaling
    LOO valid
    Default plots core.ppc_fan, core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, mmm.decomposition, mmm.response_curves, mmm.marginal_cost
    Resources class M (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    y_hat (time) of y Expected (or predictive) KPI over the panel dims and time
    contributions (component, time) of y Every channel, the baseline, trend, seasonality and each control; they sum to y_hat

    Derived quantities (outputs.derived)

    Name Dims Units Cached Description
    contributions (sample, channel, time) target fit Channel, baseline, trend, seasonality and control contributions over the fit window per thinned draw (panel dims included)
    response_curves (sample, channel, multiplier) target fit Total contribution per spend multiplier and channel (and geo) per thinned draw (Guided-mode slider grids, budget optimisation)
    marginal_cost (sample, channel) spend per target fit Extra spend per extra unit of the KPI at current spend

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    adstock AdstockSettings {"kind": "geometric", "l_max": 8, "normalize": true} basic
    saturation SaturationSettings {"kind": "logistic"} basic
    channels map of ChannelSettings – advanced Per-channel adstock/saturation overrides (channel label -> settings)
    trend TrendSettings {"kind": "linear", "n_changepoints": 10, "changepoint_range… basic
    seasonality SeasonalitySettings {"yearly_order": 2, "monthly_order": null, "weekly_order": … basic
    hierarchy HierarchySettings {"pool_over": [], "media_by_geo": false, "media_geo_sigma":… basic
    controls list of string (optional) null advanced Control variables (default: every other numeric variable over time)
    frequency W or D or M (optional) null advanced Data frequency: W (weekly), D (daily) or M (monthly); default: read from the time labels
    new_levels pooled or hyperprior or zero or error pooled advanced How a geo or product unseen at fit is scored: pooled (the overall level and average channel effects), hyperprior (a level drawn from the fitted spread, so its range is wider), zero (no channel effects) or error (refuse)
    grid GridSettings {"max_multiplier": 2.5, "points": 26, "marginal_step": 0.01} advanced
    media_prior roi or coefficient roi advanced Parameterise channel effects by their return on spend (priors are stated in ROI, comparable across channels) or by a standardised coefficient
    priors PriorSettings {"roi": {}, "roi_default": null, "intercept": null} advanced Prior overrides (written by business-prior translation)
    likelihood normal or student_t normal advanced Observation noise: normal, or student_t for heavy-tailed outliers
    Nested settings types

    AdstockSettings¶

    Carry-over of spend into later periods (mmm-framework AdstockConfig).

    Field Type Default Description
    kind geometric or delayed or weibull or none geometric geometric: decays from the spend period; delayed: peaks a few periods later; weibull: a flexible shape; none: no carry-over
    l_max integer 8 How many periods an effect can last (the kernel length) (≥ 1, ≤ 52)
    normalize boolean true Normalise the lag weights to sum to one (the effect size stays in the channel coefficient)

    ChannelSettings¶

    Per-channel overrides of the shared adstock and saturation settings.

    Field Type Default Description
    adstock AdstockSettings (optional) null
    saturation SaturationSettings (optional) null

    GridSettings¶

    Response-curve grids cached per thinned draw (Guided-mode sliders, optimisation).

    Field Type Default Description
    max_multiplier number 2.5 Largest spend multiplier on the grid (1 = spend over the fit window, which the grid always holds) (≥ 1, ≤ 20)
    points integer 26 Grid points from 0 to max_multiplier (plus 1, today's spend, when the spacing skips it) (≥ 3, ≤ 201)
    marginal_step number 0.01 Relative spend change used for marginal cost (central difference) (> 0, ≤ 0.25)

    HierarchySettings¶

    Panel structure: the dims the KPI varies over besides time. pool_over lists the panel dims of the data (geo and/or product). Every level gets its own baseline, partially pooled towards the overall level (HierarchicalConfig.pool_across_geo/product); with media_by_geo each geo also gets its own channel effects, partially pooled across geos.

    Field Type Default Description
    pool_over list of geo or product – Panel dims of the data (geo, product); empty for one national series (max items 2)
    media_by_geo boolean false Let channel effects differ by geo (partially pooled)
    media_geo_sigma number 0.3 Prior sd of the geo deviations of log channel effects (> 0, ≤ 5)

    NormalPrior¶

    Normal(mu, sigma) on the standardised KPI scale (KPI standard deviations).

    Field Type Default Description
    mu number required ≥ -50, ≤ 50
    sigma number required > 0, ≤ 50

    PriorSettings¶

    Prior overrides; business-prior translation (translate_priors) writes them. * roi - per channel, a log-normal prior on the return on spend (mmm-framework's ROI-parameterised channel effect, roi_prior_mu/roi_prior_sigma); * roi_default - the log-normal ROI prior of channels not listed (default LogNormal(0, 1): median break-even); * intercept - the baseline level in KPI standard deviations from the mean.

    Field Type Default Description
    roi map of RoiPrior – Per-channel log-normal ROI priors (channel label -> {mu, sigma})
    roi_default RoiPrior (optional) null
    intercept NormalPrior (optional) null

    RoiPrior¶

    A log-normal prior on a channel's return on spend (KPI per unit of spend over the fit window): roi ~ LogNormal(mu, sigma), so exp(mu) is the median ROI.

    Field Type Default Description
    mu number required Log of the median ROI (≥ -20, ≤ 20)
    sigma number required Spread on the log scale (> 0, ≤ 10)

    SaturationSettings¶

    Diminishing returns of (carried-over) spend (mmm-framework SaturationConfig).

    Field Type Default Description
    kind logistic or hill or michaelis_menten or tanh or root or none logistic logistic (default, most stable), hill (S-shaped), michaelis_menten, tanh, root (power curve) or none (a straight line)

    SeasonalitySettings¶

    Fourier seasonality (mmm-framework SeasonalityConfig).

    Field Type Default Description
    yearly_order integer (optional) 2 Fourier pairs of the yearly cycle (0 or null: none)
    monthly_order integer (optional) null
    weekly_order integer (optional) null Daily data only
    prior_sigma number 0.3 Prior sd of each Fourier coefficient, in KPI standard deviations (raise it for strongly seasonal categories) (> 0, ≤ 5)

    TrendSettings¶

    The slow-moving baseline (mmm-framework TrendConfig).

    Field Type Default Description
    kind none or linear or piecewise or spline or gp linear none, linear (default), piecewise (Prophet-style changepoints), spline or gp (a smooth Gaussian-process curve). Forecasts hold flexible trends at their last fitted level; a linear trend is extrapolated.
    n_changepoints integer 10 ≥ 1, ≤ 50
    changepoint_range number 0.8 > 0, ≤ 1
    n_knots integer 10 ≥ 3, ≤ 50
    growth_prior_sigma number 0.5 Prior sd of the linear slope, in KPI standard deviations over the whole history (> 0, ≤ 10)

    mmm.frequentist¶

    mmm-framework's fast frequentist marketing-mix model: adstock and saturation chosen by an out-of-sample search, a ridge solve with non-negative channel effects and bootstrap intervals; seconds instead of minutes.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference bootstrap
    Representation draws
    Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, forecast, predict
    Contributions additive
    Decision objective yes
    Fast scoring –
    Owns carryover, inverse_units, scaling
    LOO invalid: bootstrap replicates are not posterior draws
    Default plots core.ppc_fan, mmm.decomposition, mmm.response_curves, mmm.marginal_cost
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    y_hat (time) of y Expected (or predictive) KPI over the panel dims and time
    contributions (component, time) of y Every channel, the baseline, trend, seasonality and each control; they sum to y_hat

    Derived quantities (outputs.derived)

    Name Dims Units Cached Description
    contributions (sample, channel, time) target fit Channel, baseline, trend, seasonality and control contributions over the fit window per thinned draw (panel dims included)
    response_curves (sample, channel, multiplier) target fit Total contribution per spend multiplier and channel (and geo) per thinned draw (Guided-mode slider grids, budget optimisation)
    marginal_cost (sample, channel) spend per target fit Extra spend per extra unit of the KPI at current spend

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    adstock AdstockSettings {"kind": "geometric", "l_max": 8, "normalize": true} basic
    saturation SaturationSettings {"kind": "logistic"} basic
    channels map of ChannelSettings – advanced Per-channel adstock/saturation overrides (channel label -> settings)
    trend TrendSettings {"kind": "linear", "n_changepoints": 10, "changepoint_range… basic
    seasonality SeasonalitySettings {"yearly_order": 2, "monthly_order": null, "weekly_order": … basic
    hierarchy HierarchySettings {"pool_over": [], "media_by_geo": false, "media_geo_sigma":… basic
    controls list of string (optional) null advanced Control variables (default: every other numeric variable over time)
    frequency W or D or M (optional) null advanced Data frequency: W (weekly), D (daily) or M (monthly); default: read from the time labels
    new_levels pooled or hyperprior or zero or error pooled advanced How a geo or product unseen at fit is scored: pooled (the overall level and average channel effects), hyperprior (a level drawn from the fitted spread, so its range is wider), zero (no channel effects) or error (refuse)
    grid GridSettings {"max_multiplier": 2.5, "points": 26, "marginal_step": 0.01} advanced
    estimator ridge or constrained ridge advanced ridge (closed form, non-negative channel effects) or constrained (a convex program; needs the optional cvxpy dependency)
    bootstrap integer 200 basic Bootstrap replicates (the 'draws' of every output) (≥ 20, ≤ 5000)
    search_budget integer 200 advanced Adstock/saturation candidates evaluated by the transform search (≥ 10, ≤ 5000)
    ridge_alpha number 1.0 advanced Fallback L2 penalty on the standardised design (> 0, ≤ 1000000.0)
    Nested settings types

    AdstockSettings¶

    Carry-over of spend into later periods (mmm-framework AdstockConfig).

    Field Type Default Description
    kind geometric or delayed or weibull or none geometric geometric: decays from the spend period; delayed: peaks a few periods later; weibull: a flexible shape; none: no carry-over
    l_max integer 8 How many periods an effect can last (the kernel length) (≥ 1, ≤ 52)
    normalize boolean true Normalise the lag weights to sum to one (the effect size stays in the channel coefficient)

    ChannelSettings¶

    Per-channel overrides of the shared adstock and saturation settings.

    Field Type Default Description
    adstock AdstockSettings (optional) null
    saturation SaturationSettings (optional) null

    GridSettings¶

    Response-curve grids cached per thinned draw (Guided-mode sliders, optimisation).

    Field Type Default Description
    max_multiplier number 2.5 Largest spend multiplier on the grid (1 = spend over the fit window, which the grid always holds) (≥ 1, ≤ 20)
    points integer 26 Grid points from 0 to max_multiplier (plus 1, today's spend, when the spacing skips it) (≥ 3, ≤ 201)
    marginal_step number 0.01 Relative spend change used for marginal cost (central difference) (> 0, ≤ 0.25)

    HierarchySettings¶

    Panel structure: the dims the KPI varies over besides time. pool_over lists the panel dims of the data (geo and/or product). Every level gets its own baseline, partially pooled towards the overall level (HierarchicalConfig.pool_across_geo/product); with media_by_geo each geo also gets its own channel effects, partially pooled across geos.

    Field Type Default Description
    pool_over list of geo or product – Panel dims of the data (geo, product); empty for one national series (max items 2)
    media_by_geo boolean false Let channel effects differ by geo (partially pooled)
    media_geo_sigma number 0.3 Prior sd of the geo deviations of log channel effects (> 0, ≤ 5)

    SaturationSettings¶

    Diminishing returns of (carried-over) spend (mmm-framework SaturationConfig).

    Field Type Default Description
    kind logistic or hill or michaelis_menten or tanh or root or none logistic logistic (default, most stable), hill (S-shaped), michaelis_menten, tanh, root (power curve) or none (a straight line)

    Field Type Default Description
    yearly_order integer (optional) 2 Fourier pairs of the yearly cycle (0 or null: none)
    monthly_order integer (optional) null
    weekly_order integer (optional) null Daily data only
    prior_sigma number 0.3 Prior sd of each Fourier coefficient, in KPI standard deviations (raise it for strongly seasonal categories) (> 0, ≤ 5)

    TrendSettings¶

    Field Type Default Description
    kind none or linear or piecewise or spline or gp linear none, linear (default), piecewise (Prophet-style changepoints), spline or gp (a smooth Gaussian-process curve). Forecasts hold flexible trends at their last fitted level; a linear trend is extrapolated.

    changepoint_range number 0.8 > 0, ≤ 1

    sci.areal_bym2¶

    Counts of a disease in areas (districts, counties) against their expected counts, with a covariate and area effects that borrow strength from neighbouring areas: an ICAR, a proper CAR, BYM2 (a scaled ICAR mixed with independent noise) or iid effects. Outputs the smoothed relative risk of each area, the probability that it is above 1, and the expected counts. The polygons and the graph go into the bundle for the maps.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO valid
    Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.area_map, net.graph, core.ridge
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    cases (area) of cases Cases in each area: the expected count expected * rr, or a Poisson draw
    rr (area) 1 Relative risk of each area (1 = the reference rate)
    p_exceed (area) probability 1 when rr is above exceed_threshold in a draw, else 0: the mean over draws is the probability P(rr > threshold)
    effect (area) 1 The area effect u on the log relative risk (what the covariate does not explain)

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    kind poisson or iid or icar or car or bym2 bym2 – Prior of the area effects: poisson (none), iid, icar, car (proper CAR) or bym2 (ICAR plus iid with a mixing share rho) (x-ui-level: basic)
    islands link_nearest or isolate or error link_nearest – Areas without neighbours: link_nearest links each to the area with the closest boundary; isolate keeps them alone (iid and icar only); error stops (x-ui-level: basic)
    covariate_scale number 10.0 – Divide the centred covariate by this (b1 is the effect of one unit) (> 0)
    center_covariate boolean true – Subtract the mean of the covariate
    intercept_sd number 1.0 – Prior sd of the intercept b0 (> 0)
    slope_sd number 1.0 – Prior sd of the covariate effect b1 (> 0)
    sigma_scale number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of sigma, the sd of the area effects (> 0)
    rho_alpha number 1.0 – Beta prior of rho (bym2): first shape (> 0)
    rho_beta number 1.0 – Beta prior of rho (bym2): second shape (> 0)
    exceed_threshold number 1.0 – p_exceed is the probability that rr is above this value (> 0)
    Input data contract (schema template)

    sci.circular_regression¶

    Angles (wind directions, times of day) on the circle. Regression kinds put the hour of day and the day of year into harmonic features and use a von Mises with a canonical link (or a projected normal, or a mixture of two regimes with a gate); kind activity fits a log-Fourier density per group (camera-trap times) with activity levels and overlaps. Outputs are mean directions, resultant lengths and predictive densities by block of the day or by group.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO valid
    Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.rose, sci.profile_bands, sci.field_map
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    direction_hat (obs) of direction Mean direction of the row's predictive distribution (expected), or a simulated angle (predictive), from 0 to one turn
    resultant (obs) 1 Mean resultant length of the row's predictive distribution (1: one direction, 0: no preferred direction)
    density (frame, angle) 1/unit Predictive density per unit of the direction on a grid of angles, for each block of the day (regression) or group (activity)
    mean_direction (frame) of direction Direction of the mean resultant vector of each frame
    resultant_length (frame) 1 Length of the mean resultant vector of each frame
    activity_level (frame) 1 kind activity: fraction of the day the group is active, 1 / (2 pi max f)
    overlap (frame, frame_) 1 kind activity: coefficient of overlap of the activity densities of two groups

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    kind von_mises or projected_normal or regime_mixture or activity von_mises – von_mises (canonical link), projected_normal, regime_mixture (two von Mises regimes with a gate), or activity (a log-Fourier density per group) (x-ui-level: basic)
    units degrees or radians or hours degrees – Units of the direction: degrees, radians or hours (a time of day) (x-ui-level: basic)
    group_dim string group – kind activity: the dim of the groups (species); the index variable is _idx
    daily_harmonics integer 3 – Harmonics of the hour of day (≥ 0, ≤ 8)
    annual_harmonics integer 2 – Harmonics of the day of year (≥ 0, ≤ 6)
    interaction_harmonics integer 2 – Daily harmonics multiplied by the first annual harmonic (the daily cycle changes with the season) (≥ 0, ≤ 8)
    intercept_sd number 2.0 – Prior sd of the intercepts (not used by regime_mixture) (> 0)
    coef_sd number 1.0 – Prior sd of the other coefficients (> 0)
    regime_directions_deg list of number – – regime_mixture: prior mean direction of each regime (degrees, in the units' own orientation) (min items 2, max items 2)
    regime_names list of string – – regime_mixture: names of the two regimes (min items 2, max items 2)
    regime_strength number 2.0 – regime_mixture: prior mean concentration of each regime (> 0)
    regime_daily_harmonics integer 2 – ≥ 0, ≤ 8
    regime_annual_harmonics integer 1 – ≥ 0, ≤ 6
    gate_intercept_sd number 1.5 – Prior sd of the gate intercept (> 0)
    harmonics integer 16 – activity: Fourier harmonics (≥ 1, ≤ 64)
    tau_sd number 2.0 – activity: half-normal scale of tau (> 0)
    grid_points integer 256 – activity: angles of the normalising sum (≥ 32, ≤ 4096)
    frames integer 8 – Regression kinds: blocks of the day for density and mean_direction (8: three hours each) (≥ 1, ≤ 48)
    angle_points integer 72 – Angles of the density output (≥ 8, ≤ 720)
    rows_per_frame integer 200 – Scored rows averaged per frame for the density (≥ 1, ≤ 20000)
    score_draws integer 400 – Posterior draws kept per score (evenly spaced) (≥ 1, ≤ 20000)
    Input data contract (schema template)

    sci.cmb_field¶

    Field-level inference of a masked CMB temperature map: every pixel of the sky on a periodic flat patch is sampled jointly with the bandpowers by a Wandelt-Eriksen Gibbs sampler (constrained realisations by preconditioned conjugate gradients, an inverse-gamma bandpower step and a rescaling move). Gives the Wiener-filtered map, sky draws behind the mask, a per-pixel sd and the bandpowers.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO invalid: every pixel depends on one latent sky field with tens of thousands of parameters, so pointwise leave-one-out is not defined; compare variants by their bandpowers, amplitude and tilt
    Default plots core.convergence, sci.power_spectrum, sci.field_map, sci.image_residuals, sci.ppc_image_grid
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    sky (row, col) uK Posterior draws of the beamed sky (constrained realisations; unconstrained skies with the posterior spectrum for simulate)
    temperature_hat (row, col) of temperature The sky draw (expected), plus noise with noise_sd (predictive)
    bandpower (bin) uK^2 Bandpower D_ell of each bin
    bandpower_ratio (bin) 1 Bandpower over the reference bandpower, exp(q)
    log_amplitude () 1 Log amplitude of the bandpowers relative to the reference
    tilt () 1 Tilt of the bandpowers relative to the reference, at tilt_pivot

    Derived quantities (outputs.derived)

    Name Dims Units Cached Description
    sky_moments (stat, row, col) uK fit Posterior mean (the Wiener filter averaged over the spectrum) and sd of each pixel over every kept Gibbs draw

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    pixel_arcmin number 7.5 – Side of a map pixel (arcmin) (x-ui-level: basic) (> 0, ≤ 600)
    beam_fwhm_arcmin number 5.0 – FWHM of the Gaussian beam of the map (arcmin) (≥ 0, ≤ 600)
    pixel_subsamples integer 8 – Point samples per pixel side that the map pixels average (box window; 1 = none) (≥ 1, ≤ 64)
    pixel_window boolean false – The data has a pixel_window(multipole) variable (for example the HEALPix window of the source map)
    bin_edges list of number – – Multipole edges of the bandpower bins (x-ui-level: basic) (min items 2, max items 101)
    projection gnomonic or flat gnomonic – gnomonic: correct the multipoles for the mean stretch of a tangent-plane projection; flat: no correction (x-ui-level: basic)
    border integer 8 – Unobserved pixels around the raster on the periodic torus (≥ 0, ≤ 128)
    ell_dense number 300.0 – Modes below this multipole get the dense CG preconditioner (≥ 0)
    n_alias integer 3 – Aliased replicas folded into the prior power (≥ 0, ≤ 6)
    mean_prior_sd number 100.0 – Prior sd of the patch mean (uK) (> 0)
    cg_tol number 1e-05 – Relative residual that stops CG (> 0, ≤ 0.1)
    cg_max_iter integer 5000 – Most CG iterations per solve (≥ 10, ≤ 100000)
    rescale boolean true – Use the non-centred rescaling move
    q_init_sd number 0.3 – Sd of the dispersed chain starts (≥ 0, ≤ 3)
    tilt_pivot number 500.0 – Pivot multipole of the tilt (> 0)
    tilt_max_ell number 1450.0 – Bins with a centre at or above this are left out of the tilt (> 0)
    tilt_prior_sd number 0.5 – Prior sd of log amplitude and tilt (> 0)
    field_draws integer 40 – Sky maps drawn per score (over all chains) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000)
    Input data contract (schema template) 
    {
  "params": {
    "pixel_window": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "default": false
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "row": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Map rows (bottom up)"
      },
      "col": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Map columns"
      },
      "multipole": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Multipole ell = 0, 1, 2, ... of the reference spectrum"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "temperature": {
        "dims": [
          "row",
          "col"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow",
        "description": "CMB temperature of each pixel (uK); NaN where masked"
      },
      "noise_sd": {
        "dims": [
          "row",
          "col"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "weight",

    sci.colour_naming¶

    Colour naming in one language (World Color Survey): the probability that a speaker gives each term to each colour chip, as a softmax over quadratic CIELAB logits with zero-sum weights, pooled or with speaker-level intercepts and linear weights. Predicts new speakers and maps each term's share of speakers on the chip palette.

    sci.fisher_kpp¶

    Cell counts across a closing wound (a scratch assay) as a Fisher-KPP reaction-diffusion equation: cells move with diffusivity D, divide logistically at rate lam up to a capacity K, optionally after a start-up delay. The PDE runs inside the model from the counts at the first time; outputs are the expected density field (a kymograph over time and position) and the front speed 2 sqrt(D lam).
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO valid
    Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.profile_bands, sci.field_map
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    density (t, x) of count Cells per column: the expected count K u(x, t), or a Poisson draw
    wave_speed () um/h Speed of the travelling invasion front, 2 sqrt(D lam)

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    steps_per_hour integer 10 – Explicit Euler steps per hour; more steps are slower but stable for a larger diffusivity (x-ui-level: basic) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000)
    delay boolean true – Multiply movement and growth by tanh(beta t): the cells start slowly after the scratch (x-ui-level: basic)
    max_extension integer 4 – Observation periods a forecast may reach past the last fitted time (≥ 0, ≤ 1000)
    diffusivity_median number 1000.0 – Prior median of D (um^2/h) (> 0)
    diffusivity_log_sd number 1.0 – Log-scale sd of the prior of D (> 0)
    growth_median number 0.05 – Prior median of lam (1/h) (> 0)
    growth_log_sd number 1.0 – Log-scale sd of the prior of lam (> 0)
    capacity_mu number 122.0 – Prior mean of K (cells per column) (> 0)
    capacity_sigma number 15.0 – Prior sd of K (> 0)
    delay_rate_median number 0.1 – Prior median of beta (1/h) (> 0)
    delay_rate_log_sd number 1.0 – Log-scale sd of the prior of beta (> 0)
    initial_floor number 0.1 – Smallest initial count, so an empty column can still fill (> 0)
    cfl_quantile number 0.99 – Quantile of the prior of D that must satisfy D dt / dx^2 <= 1/2 (> 0.5, < 1.0)

    sci.graphical_model¶

    Learns which variables are directly linked: partial correlations (the correlation of two variables given all the others) and the probability of an edge, P(|rho| > threshold). kind dense is a multivariate normal with an LKJ prior on the correlations (it also predicts and simulates new samples); kind neighbourhood is a sparse horseshoe regression of each variable on the others with AND/OR symmetrisation.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO valid
    Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, net.graph, sci.field_map
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    pcor (var, var_) 1 Partial correlation of each pair of variables given all the others (unit diagonal)
    edge_prob (var, var_) 1 Edge indicator per draw (|partial correlation| > threshold); its mean over the draws is the edge probability
    value (cell, var) of value dense only: the values of each cell (a draw from the model with kind predictive or mode simulate)

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    kind dense or neighbourhood dense – dense: one multivariate normal with an LKJ prior (predicts and simulates cells); neighbourhood: sparse horseshoe regressions of each variable on the others (x-ui-level: basic)
    threshold number 0.1 – Relevance threshold delta: an edge is |partial correlation| > delta (x-ui-level: basic) (> 0, < 1)
    standardise boolean true – Centre and scale each variable with the mean and sd of the fit data
    reference boolean false – The data has a known network reference(var, var_) (1 = edge) that the plots compare with (x-ui-level: basic)
    log_likelihood auto or joint or conditional auto – Pointwise log-likelihood kept for elpd_loo: joint (dense only) or conditional (each variable given the others; both kinds). auto: joint for dense, conditional for neighbourhood
    lkj_eta number 2.0 – dense: LKJ shape of the correlation prior (> 0)
    sd_rate number 1.0 – dense: rate of the Exponential prior of the standardised sds (> 0)
    mean_sd number 1.0 – dense: sd of the Normal prior of the means (> 0)
    expected_neighbours number 2.0 – neighbourhood: prior guess p0 of the neighbours of each variable (sets the global horseshoe scale) (> 0)
    slab_alpha number 2.0 – neighbourhood: c^2 ~ InvGamma(alpha, beta) (> 0)
    slab_beta number 2.0 – neighbourhood: c^2 ~ InvGamma(alpha, beta) (> 0)
    edge_rule and or or or rho and – neighbourhood: an edge when both coefficients pass the threshold (and), either one (or), or their symmetric combination (rho)

  "params": {
    "reference": {
      "type": "boolean",

    }

        "description": "Exchangeable samples (cells); new ones may be scored"
      },
      "var": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "The measured variables: the nodes of the graph"

      "value": {
        "dims": [
          "cell",

        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "description": "The measured value of each variable in each cell"
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "reference": true
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "var_": {
            "kind": "categorical",
            "policy": "fixed",
            "description": "The variables again (the second node of a pair)"
          }
        },
        "vars": {
          "reference": {
            "dims": [

            ],

    sci.ibp_features¶

    Latent binary features of small images (handwritten digits): every image is the average image plus the features it owns. A stick-breaking Indian buffet process truncated at K features, with every image's binary pattern summed out over 2^K patterns, so NUTS samples the feature images and their probabilities. Outputs are the feature images, which images own them, and completions of unseen pixels.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, predict
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO valid
    Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.field_map, sci.ppc_image_grid, sci.image_residuals
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    ink_hat (digit, y, x) of ink Expected image given the seen pixels (completion where unseen), or a draw of pattern and noise
    features (feature, y, x) ink Feature images: the ink a feature adds to (or removes from) the average image
    feature_prob (feature) 1 Probability pi_k that an image owns feature k
    owns (digit, feature) 1 Probability that each image owns each feature, given its seen pixels

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    n_features integer 8 – Truncation K: the largest number of features. Each image sums over 2^K patterns, so each extra feature doubles the cost (x-ui-level: basic) (≥ 1, ≤ 10)
    kind fixed_noise or free_noise fixed_noise – fixed_noise keeps the pixel noise at noise_sd (the notebook); free_noise learns it (x-ui-level: basic)
    noise_sd number 0.25 – Pixel noise sigma_X (ink units). It sets the resolution: a smaller value makes more features worth keeping (x-ui-level: basic) (> 0)
    alpha_shape number 1.0 – Gamma shape of the IBP mass alpha (> 0)
    alpha_rate number 1.0 – Gamma rate of the IBP mass alpha (> 0)
    feature_scale_sd number 1.0 – HalfNormal scale of sigma_A (> 0)
    start digits or default digits – digits: every chain starts at half of K random images with nu = 0.8 and no jitter (avoids the 'no features' trap); default: the jittered platform start
    score_draws integer 200 – Posterior draws (spread over the chains) per score (≥ 1, ≤ 4000)
    shown_mask boolean false – The data has a shown(digit, y, x) mask: pixels where it is False are hidden from the fit (held-out halves)
    truncation_warn number 0.05 – Warn when the posterior mean of the last feature probability is above this (> 0, < 1)

    sci.lgcp_grid¶

    A log-Gaussian Cox process for event counts on a regular space-time grid: a random-walk total per period times a smooth 2-D map (Matérn-5/2 HSGP) that can change from era to era, with negative-binomial counts. Forecasts reach at most max_extension periods past the fit.

    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –

    rate (period, row, col) of count Events per cell and period: the expected intensity, or a predictive count draw
    total (period) of count Expected events per period in the whole grid

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    max_extension integer 8 – Periods a forecast may reach past the fitted range without a refit (x-ui-level: basic) (≥ 1, ≤ 400)
    era_periods integer 4 – Periods in one era: the spatial field changes from era to era (4 quarters = one map per year) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000)
    field era_walk or static era_walk – era_walk: a new map each era (a random walk of maps); static: one map for all periods (the separable model)
    anchor busiest or first or last busiest – The era whose map gets the marginal prior; the other eras walk away from it (busiest = the fit era with the most events)
    likelihood negbin or poisson negbin –
    cell_km number 25.0 – Width of one grid cell in km (> 0)
    m_row integer 10 – HSGP basis functions along rows (≥ 2, ≤ 60)
    m_col integer 14 – HSGP basis functions along columns (≥ 2, ≤ 60)
    c number 1.5 – HSGP boundary factor (> 1.0, ≤ 5.0)

    ell_upper_km number 100.0 – 95% quantile of the lengthscale prior (> 0)
    alpha_sigma number 1.5 – Sd of the log total per period (centred on the fit mean) (> 0)
    sigma_g_scale number 0.5 – Half-normal scale of the RW step (> 0)
    eta0_scale number 2.0 – Half-normal scale of the anchor map (> 0)

    sci.network_latent_space¶

    An undirected graph (who works with whom) as one Bernoulli tie for each pair of nodes. The log odds add pair covariates (homophily), a sociality effect per node and, for kind latent_space, minus the distance between latent positions. Outputs are the tie probability of every pair, the positions (aligned by Procrustes), the sociality, simulated graphs and their statistics.

              "cov"
            ],
            "dtype": "float64",
            "description": "Covariates of each pair, for example 1 when the two nodes are in the same group"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "node_groups": true
      },
      "merge": {
        "vars": {
          "node_group": {
            "dims": [
              "node"
            ],
            "dtype": "int64",
            "role": "constant",
            "description": "A group code of each node, used for colours in plots"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

    sci.phylo_regression¶

    A regression of one trait of species on other traits whose residuals are correlated by a phylogeny: i.i.d., Brownian motion, Pagel's lambda or Ornstein-Uhlenbeck on the shared branch length of the tree. Predicts a missing trait from relatives and stores the leave-one-out conditional log density for elpd_loo.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO valid
    Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.phylogeny
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    trait (species) of trait The trait of each species predicted from its relatives (Gaussian conditioning on the other species; the median when the trait is logged), or a draw with the conditional noise
    slope (predictor) 1 Slope of each predictor (sd of the trait per sd of the predictor when standardised)

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    kind iid or brownian or lambda or ou lambda – Residual correlation: iid (no tree), brownian (Brownian motion on the tree), lambda (Pagel's lambda: tree part plus a species part) or ou (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck) (x-ui-level: basic)
    predictors list of string – – Names of the predictor variables on the species dim (x-ui-level: basic) (max items 16)
    log_target boolean true – Take the log of the trait (it must be positive)
    log_predictors boolean true – Take the log of each predictor (they must be positive)
    standardise boolean true – Centre and scale the trait and the predictors by the fitted species (the slopes are then in sd of the trait per sd of the predictor)
    intercept_sd number 1.0 – Prior sd of the intercept (> 0)
    slope_sd number 0.5 – Prior sd of each slope (> 0)
    sigma_rate number 1.0 – Rate of the exponential prior of sigma (> 0)
    lambda_alpha number 1.0 – Beta prior of lambda: first shape (> 0)
    lambda_beta number 1.0 – Beta prior of lambda: second shape (> 0)
    ou_parameterisation rate or variance rate – ou: put the prior on the Brownian rate eta2*rho (rate, recommended) or on eta2 and rho (variance)
    rate_sd number 1.0 – ou (rate): HalfNormal sd of eta2*rho (> 0)
    rho_sd number 5.0 – ou: HalfNormal sd of rho (pull to the optimum) (> 0)
    eta2_sd number 5.0 – ou (variance): HalfNormal sd of eta2 (> 0)
    jitter number 1e-06 – ou: added to the diagonal of K (≥ 0, ≤ 0.01)
    Input data contract (schema template)

    "predictors": {

  "template": {

        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Every node of the tree (tips and internal nodes)"
      }
    },

        ],

        "dims": [

    sci.storm_localisation¶

    Single-molecule localisation microscopy (STORM/PALM): finds isolated spots in raw EMCCD frames and fits each with a pixel-integrated Gaussian PSF on a background, with Poisson counts after the camera's photon-transfer calibration. Outputs are positions with nm error bars, photons, the PSF width, a super-resolved render and the fitted patches.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, predict
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO valid
    Default plots core.convergence, sci.point_pattern, sci.image_residuals, sci.field_map
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    x (spot) nm Column position of each spot
    y (spot) nm Row position of each spot
    photons (spot) photons Photons that each molecule emitted into the frame
    background (spot) photons/px Background at the centre of each patch
    psf_sd (spot) nm PSF sd of each spot
    render (render_y, render_x) localisations Super-resolved image: the spots at the drawn positions, blurred by half a render pixel
    patch_fit (spot, py, px) counts Expected effective counts (photons / 2) of each fitted patch, or Poisson draws
    frames_hat (frame, row, col) of frames Camera image (ADU): the fitted spots on the background

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    pixel_nm number 100.0 – Size of one camera pixel in the sample (nm) (x-ui-level: basic) (> 0)
    kind flat or plane flat – Background in each patch: flat (one value) or plane (a value and a slope in x and y) (x-ui-level: basic)
    offset_adu number (optional) null – Camera offset (ADU). Set it with scale_adu; unset, both come from the photon-transfer curve of the frames
    scale_adu number (optional) null – ADU per effective count: twice the EM gain (the photon-transfer slope)
    max_spots integer 200 – Isolated spots fitted, evenly spaced in frame order (x-ui-level: basic) (≥ 1, ≤ 5000)
    threshold_sd number 5.0 – Detection threshold (robust noise sds) (> 0)
    smooth_px number 1.0 – Gaussian smoothing before detection (px) (> 0)
    patch_px integer 11 – Side of each fitted patch (odd, px) (≥ 5, ≤ 31)
    min_blob_px integer 13 – Fewest pixels of a fitted blob (≥ 1)
    max_blob_px integer 39 – Most pixels of a fitted blob (≥ 1)
    amplitude_band list of any [0.0, 1.0] – Quantile band of blob amplitude that is fitted (0, 1: every isolated blob) (min items 2, max items 2)
    photons_median number 1500.0 – Prior median of the photons per spot (> 0)
    photons_log_sd number 1.0 – Log-scale prior sd of the photons (> 0)
    psf_sd_px number 1.0 – Prior median of the PSF sd (px) (> 0)
    psf_log_sd number 0.2 – Log-scale prior sd of the PSF sd (> 0)
    position_sd_px number 2.0 – Prior sd of the position around the blob centre (px) (> 0)
    background_photons number (optional) null – Prior median of the background (photons per pixel); unset: twice the median effective count of the movie
    background_log_sd number 0.5 – Log-scale prior sd of the background (> 0)
    gradient_sd number 0.05 – Prior sd of the background slopes (log per px; kind plane) (> 0)
    score_draws integer 40 – Posterior draws in each score (over all chains) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000)
    ppc_draws integer 20 – Predictive patch draws kept in the bundle (0: none) (≥ 0, ≤ 200)
    render_px_nm number 16.0 – Pixel size of the super-resolved render (nm; the render of score_draws draws must stay within 50,000,000 values) (≥ 1.0)

    sci.strong_lens¶

    A pixel forward model of a galaxy-scale strong gravitational lens: a singular isothermal ellipsoid with external shear traces every pixel to a Sersic source; the lens light, a PSF and correlated noise are modelled; the light amplitudes are integrated out. Gives the Einstein radius, the unlensed source and critical curves. Reads plain or tree datasets (the PSF from a /psf node).
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO invalid: the light amplitudes are integrated out over all pixels and the whitened noise couples neighbouring pixels, so pointwise leave-one-out is not defined
    Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.field_map
    Resources class M (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    model_image (row, col) of image Expected image (lens light, lensed source, sky, PSF), or a simulated observation with noise
    source (source_row, source_col) of image The unlensed source (parametric Sersic of each draw) on a source-plane grid
    einstein_radius () arcsec Einstein radius of the isothermal ellipsoid
    einstein_mass () solar_mass Mass inside the Einstein radius (needs z_lens and z_source)

    Derived quantities (outputs.derived)

    Name Dims Units Cached Description
    critical_curves (sample, curve_point) arcsec fit Tangential critical curve (image plane), its caustic and the cut (source plane) for posterior draws, in arcsec and grid pixel indices

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    pixel_scale number 0.05 – Pixel size in arcsec (> 0, ≤ 10)
    subsample integer 2 – Rays per pixel along each axis (sub-pixel sampling) (≥ 1, ≤ 4)
    lens_light_components integer 2 – Concentric Sersic profiles for the lens galaxy's light (≥ 0, ≤ 2)
    external_shear boolean true – Add an external shear to the lens
    noise_correlation number 0.0 – Lag-one correlation of the noise between neighbouring pixels (separable rows x columns; drizzled images have about 0.2). 0 treats pixels as independent (≥ 0.0, < 0.45)
    fit_noise_scale boolean true – Scale the noise map by a free factor
    use_mask boolean false – The data has a bool mask(row, col) of pixels
    psf_tolerance number 0.001 – Relative error allowed in the separable PSF expansion (> 0, < 1)
    psf_max_rank integer 12 – Most separable PSF terms (≥ 1, ≤ 40)
    psf_source auto or tree auto – Where the PSF comes from: 'auto' uses the /psf node of a tree dataset when there is one, else the flat psf variable (which the input then needs); 'tree' reads it only from the /psf node, so the flat input needs no psf
    theta_e_median number 1.0 – Prior median of the Einstein radius (> 0)
    theta_e_log_sd number 0.5 – Prior sd of log Einstein radius (> 0)
    mass_center_sd number 0.1 – Prior sd of the mass centre (> 0)
    light_center_sd number 0.1 – Prior sd of the light centre (> 0)
    ellipticity_sd number 0.2 – Prior sd of ellipticity components (> 0)
    shear_sd number 0.05 – Prior sd of the shear components (> 0)
    light_size_medians list of any [0.5, 1.5] – Prior medians of the lens-light half-light radii (min items 2, max items 2)
    source_size_median number 0.2 – Prior median source radius (> 0)
    source_offset_sd number 0.3 – Prior sd of the source position (> 0)
    noise_scale_log_sd number 0.2 – Prior sd of log noise scale (> 0)
    theta_e_start number (optional) null – Start the optimisation at this Einstein radius instead of the radius of the ring found in the light-subtracted image
    n_starts integer 5 – Starts of the full-model optimisation (source positions) (≥ 1, ≤ 9)
    max_iter integer 3000 – Iterations per optimisation (≥ 10, ≤ 100000)
    source_grid integer 30 – Source-plane grid side (pixels) (≥ 4, ≤ 128)
    source_half_width number 0.45 – Half-width of the source-plane grid (arcsec) (> 0)
    curve_points integer 128 – Points per critical curve (≥ 16, ≤ 2048)
    curve_draws integer 100 – Posterior draws with cached critical curves (≥ 1, ≤ 2000)
    z_lens number (optional) null – Lens redshift (for the mass)
    z_source number (optional) null – Source redshift (for the mass)
    h0 number 70.0 – Hubble constant (km/s/Mpc) (> 0)
    omega_m number 0.3 – Matter density (flat LCDM) (> 0, < 1)
    Input data contract (schema template) 
    {
  "params": {
    "use_mask": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "default": false
    },
    "psf_source": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "auto",
        "tree"
      ],
      "default": "auto"
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "row": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "description": "Image rows (row 0 at the bottom)"
      },
      "col": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "description": "Image columns"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "image": {
        "dims": [
          "row",
          "col"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow",
        "description": "Surface brightness of each pixel (for example electrons/s)"
      },
      "weight": {
        "dims": [
          "row",
          "col"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "weight",
        "description": "Inverse variance of each pixel; 0 leaves the pixel out"
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "psf_source": "auto"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "psf_row": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "description": "Rows of the PSF kernel"
          },
          "psf_col": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "description": "Columns of the PSF kernel"
          }
        },
        "vars": {
          "psf": {
            "dims": [
              "psf_row",

            ],

            "role": "constant",

          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "use_mask": true
      },
      "merge": {
        "vars": {
          "mask": {
            "dims": [
              "row",
              "col"
            ],
            "dtype": "bool",
            "role": "mask",
            "description": "True where the pixel is used in the fit"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]

    sci.traction_force¶

    Traction force microscopy: recovers the 2-D traction field under a cell from the displacement field of the gel. A Gaussian prior in Fourier space (white, squared exponential or Matern spectrum); NUTS on the hyperparameters with the field integrated out, then exact posterior draws of the field.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, predict
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO invalid: the likelihood is a potential over Fourier modes of the whole raster; pixels are not conditionally independent, so pointwise leave-one-out is not defined
    Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.vector_field
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    traction (component, row, col) Pa Joint posterior draws of the traction field
    displacement_hat (component, row, col) of displacement Displacement of each traction draw (expected), plus noise (predictive)
    strain_energy () fJ Elastic energy the cell put into the gel, inside the force mask
    contractility () uN Sum of the forces towards the force epicentre, inside the mask

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    grid_um number 1.0 – Grid spacing of the displacement raster (um) (> 0)
    young_pa number 10000.0 – Young's modulus of the gel (Pa) (> 0)
    poisson number 0.49 – Poisson ratio of the gel (≥ 0, < 0.5)
    young_cv number 0.0 – Relative uncertainty of Young's modulus (lognormal sd); 0 = known exactly (≥ 0, ≤ 1)
    prior white or smooth or matern matern – Prior spectrum of the tractions: white (Tikhonov), smooth (squared exponential) or matern ((1 + k^2 l^2)^-alpha)
    noise_um number 0.01 – Prior median of the noise sd (um) (> 0)
    traction_pa number 300.0 – Prior median of the traction scale (Pa) (> 0)
    lengthscale_um number 5.0 – Prior median of the length scale (um; smooth and matern) (> 0)
    field_draws integer 100 – Traction fields drawn per score (over all chains) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000)
    force_mask boolean false – The data has a force_mask(row, col) variable: strain energy and contractility are summed inside it (else over the whole grid)
    Input data contract (schema template)

  "params": {
    "force_mask": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "default": false
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "component": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      },
      "row": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed"
      },
      "col": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "displacement": {
        "dims": [
          "component",

        "description": "Displacement of the gel surface (x and y components)"
      }
    }

        }
      }

    sci.turing_pattern¶

    Turing patterns: recovers the reaction and diffusion rates of a Schnakenberg activator-substrate system from early images of a growing pattern. The likelihood is exact for the linearised dynamics (independent complex Gaussian Fourier modes, a Woodbury identity per wavenumber). Gives the dispersion relation, the pattern wavelength, P(Turing conditions hold) and simulated patterns from a spectral solver.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO valid
    Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.field_map, sci.ppc_image_grid, sci.profile_bands
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    pattern (t, y, x) of activator Activator field at the requested times: a draw given the fitted images (predict), or a new pattern from the nonlinear solver (simulate)
    settled (y, x) of activator Simulate only: the pattern of each run at settle_time
    growth (wavenumber) 1/time Dispersion relation: growth rate Re lambda(k) of a mode with wavenumber k
    p_turing () probability 1 when the Turing conditions hold for the draw (the mean is the probability)
    wavelength () length Wavelength 2 pi / k_m of the fastest-growing mode
    turing_space (b_supply, a_supply) probability 1 where the supply rates (a, b) are Turing unstable at the draw's diffusion ratio (the mean is P(Turing))

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    box_length number 100.0 – Side of the square image in the length unit of the model (the activator diffuses with D = 1 in these units) (x-ui-level: basic) (> 0)
    k2_max number 1.5 – Use only the Fourier modes with |k|^2 below this value; faster modes have decayed below the camera noise (x-ui-level: basic) (> 0)
    max_extension integer 2 – Image times a prediction may reach past the last fitted time (the linear theory holds only while the pattern is small) (≥ 0, ≤ 100)
    d_median number 10.0 – Prior median of the diffusion ratio d (> 0)
    d_log_sd number 1.0 – Log-scale sd of the prior of d (> 0)
    initial_noise_median number 0.001 – Prior median of the initial noise sd s0 (> 0)
    camera_noise_median number 0.001 – Prior median of the camera noise sd sigma (> 0)
    field_draws integer 40 – Posterior draws per score (over all chains) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000)
    simulate_draws integer 4 – Nonlinear simulations per simulate score (each one is a full PDE run) (≥ 1, ≤ 200)
    simulate_dt number (optional) null – Time step of the spectral solver in simulate (default: min(0.025, 0.1 / (g (1 + s^2))))
    settle_time number 300.0 – Time of the settled pattern in simulate (> 0, ≤ 5000.0)
    wavenumber_max number 1.2 – Largest wavenumber of the dispersion relation output (> 0)
    wavenumber_points integer 120 – Points of the dispersion relation output (≥ 10, ≤ 2000)
    a_max number 0.6 – Largest supply rate a of the Turing-space map (> 0)
    b_max number 3.0 – Largest supply rate b of the Turing-space map (> 0)
    supply_points integer 60 – Grid points along a and b of the Turing-space map (≥ 5, ≤ 300)
    precondition boolean true – Sample a parameterisation whitened at the posterior mode (Laplace approximation); the model is the same. False samples the notebook's parameters directly (needs a long warm-up, for example tune 1500)
    Input data contract (schema template) 
    {
  "params": {
    "max_extension": {
      "type": "integer",
      "default": 2
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "t": {
        "kind": "float",
        "policy": "extend",
        "ordered": true,
        "max_extension": "{max_extension}",
        "description": "Time since the uniform state was perturbed"
      },
      "y": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Pixel row"
      },
      "x": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Pixel column"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "activator": {
        "dims": [
          "t",
          "y",
          "x"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "description": "Activator concentration in each pixel (early, small pattern)"
      }
    }
  }
}

    {
  "params": {
    "target": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "y"
    },
    "rows": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "required": true
    },
    "time_dim": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "time"
    },
    "time_kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "time",
        "integer",
        "index",
        "none"
      ],
      "default": "time"
    },
    "new_levels": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "pooled",
        "zero",
        "error"
      ],
      "default": "pooled"
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "{*rows as d}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "{new_levels}"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "{target}": {
        "dims": "{rows}",
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow"
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "time"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "time",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "integer"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "index"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "index",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

    ColumnsSettings¶

    ConformalUncertainty¶

    Split-conformal prediction intervals (representation interval, never draws). A calibration fraction of the training rows is held out (the most recent periods of time_dim for calibration_by: last, a seeded random subset for random); the interval is point ± q where q is the ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))-th smallest absolute calibration residual. refit refits the point model on all rows afterwards (sharper, but the finite-sample guarantee then only holds approximately).

    Field Type Default Description
    kind conformal conformal
    alpha number 0.1 > 0, < 1
    calibration number 0.2 ≥ 0.05, ≤ 0.5
    calibration_by last or random last
    refit boolean false

    Input data contract (schema template) 
    {
  "params": {
    "target": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "y"
    },
    "rows": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "required": true
    },
    "time_dim": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "time"
    },
    "time_kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "time",
        "integer",
        "index",
        "none"
      ],
      "default": "time"
    },
    "new_levels": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "pooled",
        "zero",
        "error"
      ],
      "default": "pooled"
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "{*rows as d}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "{new_levels}"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "{target}": {
        "dims": "{rows}",
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow"
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "time"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "time",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "integer"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "index"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "index",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

    tabular.hierarchical_glm¶

    A hierarchical generalised linear model in long layout: group intercepts (and optional slopes) partially pooled towards a population mean that may depend on group-level covariates. Unseen groups are drawn from the fitted hyperprior.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, predict
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO valid
    Default plots core.ppc, core.convergence, core.posterior_forest
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    y_hat (obs) of y Expected response (mean) or a predictive draw per observation

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    group_dim string county – The grouping dim (index var: _idx)
    family normal or student_t or poisson or bernoulli normal – Likelihood family (its canonical link)
    covariates list of string [] – Observation-level predictors over obs (max items 256)
    varying_slopes list of string [] – Covariates whose slope varies by group (max items 32)
    group_covariates list of string [] – Group-level predictors of the group intercept (max items 64)
    centered boolean false – Centred group effects (non-centred default)
    intercept_sigma number 2.0 – Prior sd of the population intercept (> 0)
    group_sigma_scale number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of group sds (> 0)
    beta_sigma number 1.0 – Prior sd of the population slopes (> 0)
    noise_sigma number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of the noise sd (> 0)
    Input data contract (schema template) 
    {
  "params": {
    "group_dim": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "county"
    },
    "covariates": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "default": []
    },
    "group_covariates": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "default": []
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "layout": "long",
    "dims": {
      "obs": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "extend"
      },
      "{group_dim}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "hyperprior"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "obs"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target"
      },
      "{group_dim}_idx": {
        "dims": [
          "obs"
        ],
        "dtype": "int64",
        "role": "index",
        "index_of": "{group_dim}"
      },
      "{*covariates as v}": {
        "dims": [
          "obs"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "covariate"
      },
      "{*group_covariates as v}": {
        "dims": [
          "{group_dim}"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "covariate"
      }
    }
  }
}

    ts.ardl¶

    statsmodels ARDL: the result regressed on its own lags and current and past values of drivers by least squares; optional lag selection by information criterion; one model per series of a panel; forecasts need future drivers.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference point
    Representation quantiles
    Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO invalid: statsmodels estimates are maximum-likelihood or least-squares point estimates without posterior draws; use holdout or backtest metrics instead of LOO
    Default plots core.ppc_fan, core.fit_vs_actual, core.residuals_over_time
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    y_hat (t) of y Prediction-interval quantiles of y: one-step-ahead inside the fitted range, a multi-step forecast after it

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    exog list of string required basic Driver variables (at least one); their future values are needed for forecasts (min items 1, max items 64)
    series_dims list of string – basic Panel dims (geo, product, ...): one model per series cell. Empty for a single series. (max items 4)
    quantiles list of number – advanced Quantiles of the prediction intervals (must include 0.05, 0.5 and 0.95) (min items 3, max items 16)
    time_kind time or integer time advanced Whether the time index holds dates ('time') or period numbers ('integer')
    lags integer 1 – Past values of the result to use (≥ 0, ≤ 12)
    order integer 1 – Past values of each driver to use (0 = same period only) (≥ 0, ≤ 12)
    trend n or c or t or ct c – n none, c constant, t trend, ct both
    auto boolean false – Choose lags and driver orders per series by an information criterion (up to lags/order)
    ic aic or bic or hqic aic – Criterion for auto
    causal boolean false advanced Use only past values of the drivers (no same-period effect)
    Input data contract (schema template) 
    {
  "params": {
    "series_dims": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "default": []
    },
    "time_kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "time",
        "integer"
      ],
      "default": "time"
    },
    "exog": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "default": []
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "t": {
        "kind": "time",
        "policy": "extend"
      },
      "{*series_dims as d}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "{*series_dims}",
          "t"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "forbid"
      },
      "{*exog as x}": {
        "dims": [
          "{*series_dims}",
          "t"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "covariate",
        "future_required": true
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "integer"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "t": {
            "kind": "integer"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

    ts.gaussian_hmm¶

    A K-state Gaussian hidden Markov model over padded sequences (e.g. animal tracks). Hidden states are marginalised with the forward algorithm; forecasts and filters start from the stored terminal state.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, filter, forecast, predict
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO invalid: the HMM likelihood is a potential over whole sequences; steps within a sequence are dependent, so pointwise leave-one-out is not defined
    Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    y_hat (animal, step) of y One-step-ahead expected value or predictive draw of y
    state_prob (animal, step, state) probability Hidden-state probabilities (predicted, or filtered in filter mode)

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    n_states integer 2 – Number of hidden states K (≥ 2, ≤ 8)
    mu_center number 0.0 – Prior mean of the state means
    mu_sigma number 2.0 – Prior sd of the state means (> 0)
    sigma_scale number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of the emission sds (> 0)
    stickiness number 2.0 – Extra Dirichlet weight on staying in the same state (≥ 0, ≤ 1000)
    pi_concentration number 1.0 – Dirichlet weight of pi (> 0)
    identification relabel or ordered relabel – relabel: sort states by mean after sampling; ordered: ordered prior

        ],

    ts.hsgp_trend¶

    A smooth Hilbert-space GP trend with optional linear drift and Fourier seasonality for one regular time series (Mauna-Loa style). Forecasts reach at most max_extension periods past the fit; further horizons need a refit.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference mcmc
    Representation draws
    Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO valid
    Default plots core.ppc_fan, core.convergence, core.posterior_forest
    Resources class S (min S)

    Outputs

    Output Dims Units Description
    y_hat (t) of y The series: expected value (trend + seasonality) or a predictive draw
    trend (t) of y The long-term component (intercept + drift + GP), no seasonality

    Settings (model.settings)

    Field Type Default Level Description
    max_extension integer 24 – Periods a forecast may reach past the fitted range without a refit; sizes the HSGP domain (x-ui-level: basic) (≥ 1, ≤ 10000)
    kernel expquad or matern52 or matern32 expquad – Covariance kernel of the smooth trend
    m integer 30 – Number of HSGP basis functions (≥ 4, ≤ 400)
    c number 1.5 – Boundary factor (L = c on the scaled axis) (> 1.0, ≤ 5.0)
    lengthscale_mu number 0.4 – Median of the lengthscale prior on the scaled axis [-1, 1] (> 0)
    lengthscale_sigma number 0.5 – Log-scale sd of the lengthscale (> 0)
    eta_sigma number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of the GP amplitude (> 0)
    linear_trend boolean true –
    intercept_sigma number 1.0 – > 0
    slope_sigma number 1.0 – > 0
    season_period number (optional) 12.0 – Seasonal period in periods of t (12 for monthly data)
    season_order integer 3 – Fourier order of the seasonality (≥ 0, ≤ 20)
    season_sigma number 0.5 – > 0
    noise_sigma number 0.5 – > 0
    Input data contract (schema template) 
    {
  "params": {
    "max_extension": {
      "type": "integer",
      "default": 24
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "t": {
        "kind": "time",
        "policy": "extend",
        "max_extension": "{max_extension}"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "t"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow"
      }
    }
  }
}

    ts.var¶

    statsmodels VAR(p) by least squares with the lag order chosen by AIC/BIC/HQIC/FPE; joint forecasts with intervals, orthogonalised impulse responses with 95% bands, forecast-error variance decomposition and pairwise Granger causality tests.
    Version 1.0.0
    Inference point
    Representation quantiles
    Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict
    Contributions none
    Decision objective –
    Fast scoring –
    Owns –
    LOO invalid: statsmodels estimates are maximum-likelihood or least-squares point estimates without posterior draws; use holdout or backtest metrics instead of LOO
    Default plots core.ppc_fan, core.fit_vs_actual, core.residuals_over_time
    Resources class S (min S)

    y_hat (t) of y Prediction-interval quantiles of y: one-step-ahead inside the fitted range, a multi-step forecast after it

    series_dims list of string – basic Panel dims (geo, product, ...): one model per series cell. Empty for a single series. (max items 4)
    quantiles list of number – advanced Quantiles of the prediction intervals (must include 0.05, 0.5 and 0.95) (min items 3, max items 16)

    ts.vecm¶

    statsmodels VECM (Johansen maximum likelihood) for trending series tied together in the long run; the cointegration rank comes from the Johansen trace or max-eigenvalue test unless set; stores alpha/beta, the rank test table, impulse responses, FEVD and Granger tests.

    Inference point

    Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict
